author: Nomadcxx
title: shell: TestCaffeineFailureUpdatesOpenScreensaverSettings can hang the suite under load (Registry mutex starvation)
text:
## Symptom
`internal/shell` full suite (`go test -count=1 -timeout 300s ./internal/shell`) intermittently hangs forever at `TestCaffeineFailureUpdatesOpenScreensaverSettings` when machine load is high (load avg >= ~6). Reproduced 2x on branch `feat/files-open-error`, and once on control branch `feat/files-crumb-jump` (no shell changes) -> not branch-specific. Passes in isolation (0.155s) and full suite passes at load < 2 (63-66s).

## Evidence (SIGQUIT dump)
- Test's own `waitFor` parked in `internal/sync.(*Mutex).lockSlow` on its Registry `r.mu` for 4m+.
- Many goroutines of the same Registry (surfaceFrameLoop x4, relayWalls/Media/AudioOSD/BrightnessOSD/Tooltips) queued on the same mutex.
- Mutex holder parked in a channel op while holding `r.mu`; a sibling registry logged "shell: closing without r.mu; a handler panic left it held" (registry.go:1919) at the same minute.

## Suspect
A handler path publishes to a panel host's full/unbuffered channel while holding `r.mu`; with `Registry.Close()` closing `r.closed` first (registry.go:1913) the publisher can still block, starving the mutex.

## Repro
Run `GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -count=1 -timeout 300s ./internal/shell` in a loop while the machine is loaded (e.g. two suites concurrently).

Related: surfaced repeatedly while landing the file-browser polish commission PRs (docs/plans/2026-10-06-file-browser-polish-commission.md).
